declared.title: Learning from My Success and from Others' Failure: Evidence from Minimally Invasive Cardiac Surgery
declared.foundIn: Crossref search « learning from my success and from others failure minimally invasive cardiac surgery » (2026-11-23)

population: 71 cardiothoracic surgeons, 10 years of data, more than 6,500 operations with a new technology

findings.text: Surgeons improved more after their own successes than after their own failures, but more after colleagues' failures than after colleagues' successes

support.sentence: We find that individuals learn more from their own successes than from their own failures, but they learn more from the failures of others than from others' successes.

findings.text: Past successes and colleagues' failures helped surgeons get past their difficulty in learning from their own failures

support.sentence: We also find that individuals' prior successes and others' failures can help individuals overcome their inability to learn from their own failures.

limits: observational panel: real operations, nobody was assigned a failure; « learning » is the change in later outcomes
one specialty, one new technology, 71 surgeons; the exact definition of a failure not read (full text refused)
co-author Francesca Gino had other papers retracted from 2023 for data problems; this one carries no notice (checked by the writer and the blind review)
